title: Kellmouth Regional Transit: long-range financial outlook
confid: Prepared for the board of directors

cover.title: Keeping Kellmouth moving: the operating reserve to FY32
cover.sub: A briefing for the board of directors and the finance committee.
cover.meta: Kellmouth Regional Transit · fictional agency · theme specimen

exec.title: The operating reserve covers service today, but falls by more than half by FY32 without action

rows.p: The reserve stands at {res}, about {months} months of operating cost, after federal relief ended. Service levels and fares have held steady for two years.
Operating cost grows about {cost_g} a year while fares and local tax grow about {rev_g}. The gap widens each year the plan is deferred.
Together the options close {close} of the annual gap, enough to hold the reserve steady. Most need board decisions this year to count in FY28.

exec.source: Source: Kellmouth Regional Transit adopted budget and financial model (fictional)

chart.title: Without action the reserve falls to {base32} by FY32, and under stress it is nearly exhausted

bullets: Baseline: ridership recovers to {rid} of pre-pandemic levels.
With options: all seven options in place by FY28.
Stress: a mild recession cuts sales tax by {cut}.

chart.source: Source: Kellmouth Regional Transit financial model (fictional)

table.title: Seven options close the gap, led by the bus network redesign

exhibit.title: Options to close the operating gap

table.callout: The first four options alone close {first4}, three quarters of the gap, and only the fare refresh changes what riders pay.
